adoption_summary.text: A creator claim reports that Microduck sold over 10,000 units in three days.
adoption_summary.uncertainty: This is a seller-associated creator claim of unit sales, not independent evidence of deliveries, active use, retention, or the identity of buyers.

build_complexity_summary.text: The platform appears technically involved to implement and operate because the described stack combines reinforcement-learning training, GPU-accelerated simulation, sim-to-real considerations, and a sensorized, multi-motor robot. No evidence states development time, team requirements, manufacturing complexity, reliability, or unit economics.
build_complexity_summary.uncertainty: Technical components justify only a qualified complexity assessment; commercial and operational build requirements remain unmeasured.

business_model_summary.text: The supplied evidence supports an offered one-time/pre-order price for the robot while describing the software stack as open source. It does not specify whether monetization extends beyond hardware sales, such as support, services, accessories, or recurring software revenue.
business_model_summary.uncertainty: The price offer supports a transactional hardware-sale interpretation but does not establish the complete commercial model or realized transactions.

competition_summary.uncertainty: No signal is classified as competition or provides substantiated competitive alternatives, differentiation, or switching behavior.

customer_summary.text: Developers are explicitly described as operators who can train, transfer, refine, and share robot behaviors. The evidence does not identify the economic buyer or distinguish purchasers from end users, hobbyists, educators, or developers.
customer_summary.uncertainty: Developer is an evidenced operator label, not a verified buyer segment or purchase decision-maker.

distribution_summary.text: The RL stack is described as being distributed through GitHub, while trained gaits can be published to the Hugging Face Hub. These are evidenced software and behavior-sharing channels, not evidence of customer-acquisition performance.
distribution_summary.uncertainty: The evidence establishes delivery/sharing mechanisms but does not establish how purchasers are acquired or the reach and conversion of these channels.

pricing_summary.text: Two product-pricing signals list Microduck at USD 399: one states USD 399 before taxes and shipping as a one-time price, and another states USD 399 for pre-order.
pricing_summary.uncertainty: These are creator/product price claims, not observed purchases. Taxes and shipping are excluded in one statement; the other is explicitly a pre-order and has no stated price period.

problem_summary.text: A documented setup friction is that the default MicroDuck reinforcement-learning setup is designed for Linux and produces a GPU error on Windows; a tutorial presents WSL as a workaround.
problem_summary.uncertainty: This is a creator-described technical compatibility issue from a tutorial, with no evidence of its prevalence, severity, or effect on purchase decisions.

revenue_summary.uncertainty: No eligible product-monetization or observed-transaction revenue signal states product or company revenue.

solution_pattern.text: Microduck is presented as a vendor-specific open-source bipedal robot platform: developers train reinforcement-learning behaviors in simulation, transfer and refine them on the robot, and can share behaviors. The described implementation includes an open-source RL stack and onboard robot hardware; this evidence does not establish a broader vendor-neutral market pattern.
solution_pattern.uncertainty: Capabilities and open-source status are primarily creator claims, and the supplied evidence concerns Microduck rather than comparable platforms.

validation_gaps: Video/channel diversity is not independent customer validation.
Validate the economic buyer, intended user segments, and whether developers are purchasers, operators, or both.
Validate the Linux/Windows setup issue across independent users, including its frequency, severity, and impact on onboarding.
Obtain independent evidence of deliveries, active use, repeat use, and buyer identities; the reported 10,000-unit figure is a seller-associated creator claim.
Establish product/company revenue, realized transaction volume, returns, and unit economics; no eligible revenue evidence is supplied.
Clarify the complete monetization structure beyond the stated robot price, including support, services, accessories, and any recurring revenue.
Measure the reach and conversion of GitHub and Hugging Face Hub distribution channels; they are not evidenced customer-acquisition channels.

Reconcile the USD 399 eligible product-pricing claims with the separate approximately USD 400 product mention in signal c918d449-b230-4433-b4cf-851b711d8389, which is classified as product_launch rather than pricing evidence.
Obtain direct competition evidence; no eligible competition signal is supplied.
Validate technical implementation, manufacturing, support, and reliability requirements beyond creator-described architecture and tutorial claims.

workflow_summary.text: The evidenced developer workflow is to clone and configure the RL environment, train a walking policy in simulation, save and inspect checkpoints, transfer/refine behaviors on the physical robot, and share creations. A separate claim describes publishing a trained gait to the Hugging Face Hub for installation on a robot.
workflow_summary.uncertainty: The workflow is assembled from creator and product descriptions; no independent evidence confirms that users complete it successfully in production.
